result.title: Learning to Reason in Real-Time
result.summary: AI agents that operate in the real world must reason correctly and on-time, yet they currently do not account for how time should alter their reasoning. Modern agents learn to do tasks in environments that are entirely synchronous: where the world waits for the agent to act before changing. A real-time environment, by contrast, changes independent of the agent. Existing approaches try to bridge this gap by imposing a ratio of thinking to acting. However, for an agent to succeed in real-time it must learn to act quickly when delay is costly and to reason longer when the benefit outweighs the missed opportunities. To this end, we introduce real-time reasoning training (RRT) as the class of training techniques for real-time reasoning agents. We develop three standard RRT techniques: (1) using real-time data, (2) decoupling acting and observing, and (3) curriculum learning in time. Together, these simple techniques substantially outperform strong baselines. Across time pressures, we outperform the strongest non-RRT baseline by an average of 33% reward on in-distribution and 55% reward on out-of-distribution tasks in two real-time environments: Frogger and Snake. These results demonstrate that we can teach agents to balance reasoning and responsiveness under real-time constraints, and that RRT opens a broad, new set of capabilities for real-time agents.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 real-time reasoning training（RRT）这一训练范式，让 agent 在实时环境中学会何时快速行动、何时延长思考，并采用实时数据、解耦行动与观察、时间课程三类技术，在 Frogger 与 Snake 上验证其优于按固定思考/行动比例分配的基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「延迟成本与思考收益」的显式权衡与 THINK/STOP 的计算分配问题同构，但属游戏 RL 设定；时间课程与快慢切换的训练方式可能可供核查能否迁移为 VLM 推理期停止或动态计算的监督线索。
